title: Understudies: Hardest Workers on Broadway?
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the world of Broadway understudies, standbys, swings, and alternates, prompted by Plaza Suite starring Sarah Jessica Parker and Matthew Broderick, whose performances were canceled due to COVID. They explain the differences between understudies (ensemble or principal backups who go on regularly), standbys (on call for one principal role), swings (cover multiple roles), and alternates (scheduled replacements). They cover Actors' Equity contracts and minimum pay, swing pay bumps, rehearsal disadvantages, preparation methods like Jay Douglas's notes, famous understudy break stories (Bernadette Peters, Anthony Hopkins, Shirley MacLaine, Sutton Foster and Cathy Violco), and the COVID-era spotlight on understudies. The episode closes with a listener mail correction about Canadian independence and the Statute of Westminster.

segments.title: Opening banter and reasons for the topic
segments.summary: Hosts open with banter, then explain they were inspired by a Broadway trip seeing Plaza Suite and by Matthew Broderick and Sarah Jessica Parker's COVID cancellations, plus an article on Broadway's unsung heroes.

segments.title: Standbys, understudies, and swings defined
segments.summary: The hosts define the standby as someone who knows a lead role fully and is on call, the understudy as a cast member who goes on regularly and covers principal or ensemble roles, and the swing as someone covering five to a dozen roles. They describe Michael McGrath as Plaza Suite's standby.

segments.title: Alternates and union contract rules
segments.summary: Alternates are scheduled replacements for certain performances. The hosts explain that Actors' Equity and producers negotiate contracts requiring understudies for most roles, with exceptions for bit players and some stars.

segments.title: Logistics of cascading cast changes and pay
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how cast injuries trigger a chain of replacements, requiring logistical juggling of swings and crew. They then cover minimum pay of about two thousand thirty four dollars a week, and swing and understudy pay bumps.

segments.title: Preparation methods and rehearsal disadvantages
segments.summary: Jay Douglas recorded performances from the audience and built dossiers; Charnell Pringle trained physically and vocally. The hosts note understudies often rehearse with worklights and no orchestra, and must match the star's performance exactly.

segments.title: Famous understudy break stories
segments.summary: Stories include Adina Menzel's fall during Wicked with Shoshana Bean stepping in, Karen Quackenbush replacing Bernadette Peters in Gypsy, and Anthony Hopkins replacing Laurence Olivier in The Dance of Death. Shirley MacLaine was cast by Alfred Hitchcock after filling in on Broadway.

segments.title: Sutton Foster, COVID, and understudy advocacy
segments.summary: Sutton Foster's COVID absence let Cathy Violco take over The Music Man, prompting a Hugh Jackman speech praising understudies. Actors' Equity's Kate Shindel criticized the lack of swings, and the Broadway League's Charlotte St. Martin apologized. The episode closes with a listener mail correction about Canada and the Statute of Westminster.
